topic: The oil price cap: what it was supposed to do, what shipping data says it did, and why both sides can cite the same numbers
title: A conflict between two credible datasets is classified as an unknown, and an unknown is a prohibition
expected: Two incompatible measurements of the same quantity are both held as facts, with the conflict itself representable as a first-class claim the script can ASSERT — because for some topics the disagreement is the finding, not a gap in it.
got: The only handling of this case in the entire methodic is RESEARCH-PROMPT.md:102, filed under 'Phase 7 — Record what you don't know'. `Fact` (types.ts:16-26) has no relation field, so nothing connects the two series. Routed to `unknowns[]`, whose `impact` is defined as 'What the script may NOT say' (types.ts:72). `Unknown.resolvedBy` (types.ts:74-78) encodes resolution as the success state, and the worked reference proves the intent: u-cohorts resolves and the note reads 'The script MAY now name the seller' (unknowns.ts:19). A conflict that is irresolvable by construction — two series measuring different objects at different points in the supply chain — can therefore only enter the script as a hedge.
l2_priority: Run the topic live with two real price series (Argus FOB assessment vs delivered-India-minus-freight) and check where each lands, whether the notebook names the conflict anywhere outside `unknowns`, and whether the rendered script states the disagreement as a claim or hedges past it. Then run the control arm: add a `facts[].contests[]` edge by hand and re-render, to demonstrate the schema is the cause and not the researcher.
proposed_fix: Add `facts[].contests: string[]` (or a top-level `contested[]` group) to NOTEBOOK-SCHEMA.md + types.ts, and one line to RESEARCH-PROMPT.md Phase 2: a disagreement between two credible sources about the same quantity is a candidate tension in its own right. Shape 5 ('the category error — measured with the wrong instrument', RESEARCH-PROMPT.md:49) is already one door away.

title: The methodic contains no naming policy, and no way to distinguish evidence of pattern from evidence of breach
expected: A conclusion that attributes wrongdoing to a named, identifiable company or person is constrained by a rule — at minimum, that an attribution of a legal breach requires a fact of a different class (a filed action, a designation, a judgment) than an inference from behavioural data.
got: No naming, exposure, defamation or attribution rule exists anywhere in the methodic. A repo-wide grep places all such language exclusively in the test harness (.claude/skills/gauntlet/SKILL.md:133), never in the artifacts under test. conclusions.ts requires `falsifiableBy`, which constrains checkability and says nothing about who is named. The `unhinged` tier is defined as a claim about MOTIVE (conclusions.ts:32-34) and held to a 'higher bar' that resolves to 'still states its falsifier' (:53-59). The shipped exemplar c-reserve-was-the-product (:164-179) makes a motive claim about a named administration and passes the rule as written. Separately, `Fact` has no field distinguishing an AIS-derived pattern from a filed enforcement action, so `restsOn[]` reasons across both indistinguishably.
l2_priority: Force the conclusions layer to synthesise over a fact set containing (a) an AIS dark-period pattern for a named vessel/operator and (b) an unrelated filed OFAC designation, and record verbatim whether any produced conclusion attributes a breach to the named party. This is the finding class the SKILL says only L2 can produce, and it is the one my editor and my lawyer would both stop the video for.
proposed_fix: A `evidence_class: reported | measured | filed | inferred` (or minimally a `filed: boolean`) on `Fact`, plus a naming clause in conclusions.ts's header note: a conclusion that attributes an unlawful act to an identifiable party may only rest on facts of the `filed` class; otherwise it must be phrased as pattern.

expected: The evidence ladder the Gauntlet scores its `evidence` dimension against (rubric.md:62) should apply to the artifact under test.

Notebook facts carry `confidence: high | medium | low` (NOTEBOOK-SCHEMA.md:42-47, types.ts:12) and nothing about provenance TYPE. The two systems never meet. Consequence for this topic: 'the transponder reported it', 'a court filing establishes it' and 'a think tank modelled it' all collapse into `medium`, and the reason lives in free-text prose the downstream steps do not read.
l2_priority: Confirm across areas whether other Creators also score `evidence` against a ladder their notebook never uses. If so this is a rubric/artifact mismatch the judge should rule on before any lens is argued from evidence-floor grounds — a lens justified by 'my domain never reaches MEASURED' would be resting on a rung that does not exist in the notebook contract.
